title: DSH skin theme
description: The complete definition of one skin. `scripts/build-skins.mjs` turns this into generated/<id>.css plus a manifest entry; no skin CSS is written by hand. Adding a skin means dropping one of these files next to a hero image and re-running the generator.

id.description: Stable identifier. Must match the file name, and is what lands in `body[data-dsh-skin]` and in the persisted setting — renaming one orphans everyone's saved preference.

name.description: Display name per locale, read straight into the skin picker.

order.description: Position in the skin picker. Curated rather than alphabetical, so a new skin can be slotted next to its siblings; leave gaps of 10 so inserting one does not renumber the rest.

appearance.description: The colour scheme this skin pins the UI to, overriding the light/dark preference while it is active. This is the real thing, not a label: the generator derives the ramp for this scheme and boot-theme sets `data-ds-dark-theme` from it.

chrome.description: Which shared component treatment the skin wears. `flat` is square, opaque and shadowless; `glass` is rounded and translucent with a soft shadow; `neon` is glass plus an accent glow. Defined once in _chrome.css.

seeds.description: The four colours the whole skin is derived from. Everything else — 73 palette steps, the brand roles, the chrome band — is computed, and the generator refuses to ship a combination that fails its readability contract.

accent.description: The skin's voice: chat bubbles, the active sidebar item, the titlebar band, primary controls.

secondary.description: The second voice: focus outlines, the titlebar's bottom edge, neon trim.

surface.description: The page background, used verbatim. Every neutral step is solved against this, so it is the one seed that reaches the screen unmodified.

text.description: Anchors the far end of the neutral ramp. Its hue and chroma survive; its lightness is re-solved to hold upstream's contrast structure.

hero.description: File name inside skins/assets/, painted behind the app frame under a veil of the surface colour. Ship at least 1536px wide.

heroFocus.description: `background-position` for the hero, e.g. '50% 33%' to keep a face in frame. Defaults to centre.

glyph.description: Emoji shown in the titlebar in place of the component's hardcoded penguin.

showBadge.description: Whether to reveal the titlebar's QQ-number badge. The number itself lives in AppFrame.tsx, so this is a show/hide switch rather than a content override.

font.description: Raw `font-family` value, for skins whose era is carried by the typeface.
